description_full: Disco Corporation manufactures and sells precision cutting, grinding, and polishing machines in Japan and internationally. The company offers precision machines include dicing saws, laser saws, grinders, polishers, wafer mounters, die separators, inspection systems, surface planers, and waterjet saws. It also provides precision processing tools, such as dicing blades, grinding wheels, and dry polishing wheels; and other products, such as accessory equipment, cut-off wheels, and related products. In addition, the company is involved in the maintenance, disassembly, and recycling of precision cutting, grinding, and polishing machines, as well as provides training services for the maintenance and operation of its machines. Further, it leases precision machines; and purchases and sells used machines. Additionally, the company manufactures and sells precision diamond abrasive tools; and offers chargeable processing services. Disco Corporation was founded in 1937 and is based in Ota, Japan.

financial_summary: Disco Corp. is a large-cap technology business with a $25.0B market cap on $2.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 76% against a 10% cost of capital — a 67-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 69% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $621M in free cash flow — roughly 23 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.99× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 19% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
